content:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected — high throttle_rate and queue_depth on dedicated-us-west (service: inference-runtime). Paging @oncall.
Maya Chen: picking this up — getting logs now. seeing 502/504 spikes from serving layer.
Tom Alvarez: I see a burst of tokens/sec from a single customer cohort, plus throttle_count jumping. Queue depth hit ~3.2k on one pool.
Alina Patel: confirmed: autoscaler didn't react quickly enough because it uses average queue_depth over 60s. we had a 30s sustained spike.
Maya Chen: immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale pool up 2x, 2) route traffic to fallback model-quantized-2 if compatible, 3) disable continuous batching for hot endpoints for a bit.
Ryan O'Connell: on it — running forced scale now: `rwi scale-pool --pool dedicated-us-west --min 6 --max 12 --force`.
Priya Singh: adding temporary route policy: `route override dedicated-us-west -> model: model-quantized-2 (fallback)` for affected customer tags.
Tom Alvarez: rolling config in prod; I can push a canary to 10% then 100%.
incident-bot: SCALE action executed by Ryan O'Connell — pool replicas increased from 3 to 8. Alerts suppressed for 10m.
Maya Chen: monitoring latency and throttle events. dashboard panels: requests/sec, tokens/sec, queue_depth, throttle_count, kv_cache_hit.
Alina Patel: quick observation: throttle_count correlates with sequence length spike. looks like a few long seq batched requests increased per-token memory causing throttles.
Ryan O'Connell: after scale, client 504s dropped by ~70% within 90s. queue_depth trend falling but still noisy. we should consider adding tokens/sec as autoscale input.
Tom Alvarez: Agreed. Current autoscaler uses queue_depth and cpu; tokens/sec gives better signal for long-seq workloads.
Priya Singh: proposing immediate alert changes to reduce noise: raise queue_depth alert threshold from 1500 -> 2200 for dedicated pools, and add a new alert for sustained tokens/sec > 250k over 30s.
Maya Chen: don't raise queue_threshold blindly — we need rate-of-change guardrail. Suggest alert variant: queue_depth > 2000 OR queue_depth_deriv > 300/sec.
Alina Patel: +1 to derivative alert. Also add `throttle_count > 5` as page condition (current pages on any throttle > 1 are noisy).
Tom Alvarez: drafting patch to alerting rules now. Will add dashboard panel showing per-pool tokens/sec and per-model seq_length histogram.
Maya Chen: action items for post-incident:
- Tom: push alert rule changes and create grafana panel (due EOD)
- Alina: update autoscaler to incorporate tokens/sec and sequence_length percentiles (PR by tomorrow morning)
- Ryan: write temporary runbook section for long-seq mitigation (disable batching, fallback model) (due today)
- Priya: contact account exec for impacted customer and sync on temporary routing (in progress)
incident-bot: NOTE: suppression window ends in 7m. Remember to re-enable pages or update thresholds before then.
Ryan O'Connell: putting a 30m suppression on non-critical alerts for dedicated-us-west while changes roll out.
Maya Chen: retrospective notes while fresh: 1) autoscaler averaging window too long for bursty long-seq workloads, 2) alert sensitivity mismatch: throttles were paged at 1 event, causing noise, 3) lack of tokens/sec signal in scaling.
Priya Singh: customer impact: affected 3 mid-tier accounts, some requests timed out for ~2-3 minutes. documented in the incident doc and pinged support.
Tom Alvarez: I'm adding a small synthetic test to run every 5m that simulates long-seq traffic and verifies autoscale reacts within 45s — will add to chaos suite.
Alina Patel: we should add a dashboard alert for KV-cache miss spikes — that may amplify token work.
Maya Chen: agreed. Also schedule a 30m postmortem sync tomorrow 10:30am PT — include product for potential API changes to limit long-seq abuse.
Ryan O'Connell: follow-up: after the change, throttle_count returned to baseline, tokens/sec back to normal. closing live incident. moving to post-incident channel for writeup.
Maya Chen: thanks team. please add PR links and dashboards to the incident doc. I'll own the postmortem timeline.
sre-rotation-bot: On-call handoff: @Maya Chen -> @Tom Alvarez at 18:00 UTC. Reminder to update handoff notes. :bell:
Tom Alvarez: taking handoff. I'll monitor for regressions and verify alert behavior after suppression window expires.
Maya Chen: final note: prefer adding `tokens_per_minute` to paging thresholds (not raw tokens/sec) — smoother and less noisy. we'll test both.
incident-bot: INCIDENT resolved — root cause: burst of long-sequence requests combined with averaging window and missing tokens/sec signal in autoscaler. Follow-ups created and assigned.
